subject: P1 INTEGRITY: cloud-lab checks are forgeable from inside the container. Student has NOPASSWD sudo in openstack-cli image and can shim /usr/bin/openstack (verified: grader-shaped call returns 'in-use' on demand); even without sudo, bash -lc sources ~/.bashrc so PATH poisoning does the same. Affects LIVE Cinder lab checks 3-6 and read-only 1-2, and blocks lab 2 (Nancy BLOCK). FIX: grade cloud state SERVER-side -- add /verify to the bc2 claim service and have lab-manager call it instead of docker exec. Container-side execCheck stays valid ONLY where the container filesystem IS the subject (linux-sandbox/missions). Also remove NOPASSWD sudo from the image unless justified.
description: [2026-07-30 15:09] CORRECTION 2026-07-30: the sudo binary-shim vector does NOT work in production -- launched containers set no-new-privileges:true + CapDrop ALL, and sudo is refused. I verified the shim with a bare docker run WITHOUT production security opts (proxy-not-the-claim error). The REAL vector, proven live in an actual launched container, is profile/PATH poisoning via ~/.bashrc, which needs no privileges. Severity stands as P1 but the mechanism was misattributed. Server-side grading fix is retained regardless: it closes the real vector AND removes the dependency on container hardening staying correct forever.
